name: monocular vision loss overview
title: Vision loss in one eye: sudden painless loss is sorted by the pupils and the fundus into central retinal artery occlusion, giant cell arteritis, optic neuritis, retinal detachment and vitreous hemorrhage; gradual loss is sorted by which part of vision goes into glaucoma, cataract and macular degeneration; each column gives the presentation, the exam finding that decides it and what to do, with glaucoma and cataract risk factors below

root.title: Vision loss in ONE eye: the problem is in FRONT of the optic chiasm
lines: ask: pain? transient, persistent or progressive? abrupt or over hours, days, weeks? all or part of the field? baseline acuity? diabetes, vascular, autoimmune, hypertension · retinopathy, glaucoma, eye surgery, contact lenses

examine: acuity · confrontation fields · swinging flashlight: RAPD (Marcus Gunn) = pupil DILATES when light moves to the bad eye → retina or optic nerve · red reflex: dull = media opacity (cornea, lens, vitreous) · pressure
PAINFUL: cornea, uveitis, acute angle closure (see the RED EYE chart)

groups.title: SUDDEN + PAINLESS: what do the pupil and the fundus show?
lines: emergency measures + ophthalmology for CRAO, ischemic optic neuropathy, GCA

groups.title: GRADUAL: which part of vision goes?
lines: refer, but not same-day unless pressure > 30

head: h
Central retinal artery occlusion
EMERGENCY: ganglion cells die
pres: case: 72, 1.5 hours, right hand motion, left 20/20
tx: • heel of hand: 10 s press, 10 s release, for 5 min

head: h
Giant cell arteritis
EMERGENCY: can blind both eyes
large + medium vessels, cranial arteries, aorta
pres: • scalp tenderness · thick, tender temporal artery
• weight loss, fever, night sweats, malaise
case: 67, pain chewing, combing hair, shoulder pain 2 months · 20/80, inferior field loss
tx: • visual symptoms: IV methylprednisolone 1 g × 3 days
~ saves the other eye, prevents stroke, aortic arch syndrome

head: h
Retinal detachment
pres: • floaters = blood from a retinal tear
case: 56, 20/20 both eyes, temporal field loss
inv: ~usually not seen with a direct ophthalmoscope

head: h
Vitreous hemorrhage
inv: fragile new vessels bleed into the vitreous

head: h
Primary open-angle glaucoma
progressive, irreversible optic neuropathy
3.54% of the world
inv: • pressure > 21 (normal 10-21; can be normal: normal-tension glaucoma)

head: h
Cataract
lens opacity · leading cause of REVERSIBLE blindness
pres: • 'second sight': lenticular myopia, better near vision
• varies with where the opacity is
inv: • dense: dull red reflex or white pupil
tx: visually significant or blocks the view of the retina → extraction + intraocular lens

head: h
Age-related macular degeneration
leading IRREVERSIBLE cause over 50
pres: • wet: choroidal new vessels bleed, leak into the macula → sudden severe drop
inv: • drusen or blood at the macula
tx: • AREDS2: vitamins C, E, lutein, zeaxanthin, zinc, copper

panels.title: Glaucoma risk factors
items: open angle: Black · high pressure · MYOPIA · eye trauma · steroids · vasospasm (Raynaud's, migraine)

panels.title: Cataract risk factors and types
items: age · genetics · trauma · steroids · eye inflammation · diabetes, metabolic
radiation · prior eye surgery · excess UV
types: posterior subcapsular · cortical · nuclear sclerosis
